Japanese: 空港が大きくなります。
Hiragana: くうこう が おおきく なります
Vocabulary: 空港 = airport; 大きい = big
Explanation: 空港 (airport) + が (subject marker) + 大きい→大きく (big→adverbial form) + なります (becomes). Literally: Airport + [subject] + big + becomes.

Japanese: 滑走路が長くなります。
Hiragana: かっそうろ が ながく なります
Vocabulary: 滑走路 = runway; 長い = long
Explanation: 滑走路 (runway) + が + 長い→長く (long→adverbial form) + なります (becomes). Literally: Runway + [subject] + long + becomes.

Japanese: 大きい飛行機も着陸できます。
Hiragana: おおきい ひこうき も ちゃくりく できます
Vocabulary: 大きい = big; 飛行機 = airplane; 着陸 = landing
Grammar: ～できます = can do; も = also/too
Explanation: 大きい飛行機 (large airplane) + も (also) + 着陸できます (can land).

Japanese: この空港はとても忙しいです。
Hiragana: この くうこう は とても いそがしい です
Romaji: Kono kūkō wa totemo isogashii desu.
Vocabulary: 空港 = airport; 忙しい = busy; とても = very
Grammar: は = topic marker; ～です = polite copula
Explanation: この空港 (this airport) + は (topic marker) + とても (very) + 忙しいです (is busy).

Japanese: この滑走路は短いです。
Hiragana: この かっそうろ は みじかい です
Vocabulary: 滑走路 = runway; 短い = short
Explanation: この滑走路 (this runway) + は + 短いです (is short).

Japanese: 滑走路は約2800メートルです。
Hiragana: かっそうろ は やく にせん はっぴゃく めーとる です
Romaji: Kassōro wa yaku nisen happyaku mētoru desu.
Vocabulary: 滑走路 = runway; 約 = approximately; メートル = metre
Explanation: 滑走路は (as for the runway) + 約 (approximately) + 2800メートルです (is 2,800 metres).

Japanese: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。
Hiragana: まいにち、にほんご を べんきょう します
Vocabulary: 毎日 = every day; 日本語 = Japanese; 勉強 = study
Grammar: を = object marker; ～します = do
Explanation: 毎日 (every day) + 日本語を (Japanese + object marker) + 勉強します (study/do studying).

Hiragana: せつめい も かきます
English: I will also write an explanation.
Vocabulary: 説明 = explanation; 書く = write
Grammar: も = also; 書きます = polite form of 書く
Explanation: 説明 (explanation) + も (also) + 書きます (write).

Hiragana: ここ に ほぞん します
Vocabulary: ここ = here; 保存 = save
Grammar: に = destination/location marker; ～します = do
Explanation: ここ (here) + に (to/in) + 保存します (save).

Japanese: このリポジトリに保存します。
Hiragana: この りぽじとり に ほぞん します
English: I'll save it in this repository.
Vocabulary: この = this; リポジトリ = repository; 保存 = save
Explanation: このリポジトリ (this repository) + に (in/to) + 保存します (save).

Hiragana: おはようございます
Vocabulary: おはよう = good morning
Explanation: A standard polite morning greeting. Use it with colleagues, neighbors, hotel staff, and people you meet in the morning.

Hiragana: こんにちは
Vocabulary: こんにちは = hello
Explanation: A standard daytime greeting. The は is written as は but pronounced wa in this greeting.

Hiragana: こんばんは
Vocabulary: こんばんは = good evening
Explanation: A standard greeting used in the evening. The final は is pronounced wa.

Japanese: ありがとうございます。
Hiragana: ありがとうございます
Vocabulary: ありがとう = thanks
Explanation: The normal polite way to thank someone in shops, restaurants, work, or everyday interactions.

Japanese: どうもありがとうございます。
Hiragana: どうも ありがとうございます
Vocabulary: どうも = very / really; ありがとう = thanks
Explanation: A warmer and stronger thank-you than ありがとうございます.

Hiragana: すみません
Vocabulary: すみません = excuse me / sorry
Explanation: Extremely useful. Use it to get attention, apologize lightly, pass someone, or even when someone helps you.

Hiragana: ごめんなさい
Vocabulary: ごめんなさい = sorry
Explanation: A direct apology. With strangers and in service situations, すみません is often more natural for small inconveniences.

Hiragana: おねがいします
Vocabulary: お願い = request
Explanation: Used when asking for something or handing something over for service. Literally, I make a request.

Japanese: よろしくお願いします。
Hiragana: よろしく おねがいします
English: Nice to meet you / I look forward to working with you.
Vocabulary: よろしく = favorably / well; お願い = request
Explanation: A very Japanese multipurpose phrase used after introductions, requests, or when starting to work with someone.

Hiragana: はじめまして
Vocabulary: はじめまして = for the first time
Explanation: Used only when meeting someone for the first time, usually followed by your name and よろしくお願いします.

Hiragana: おげんき ですか
Vocabulary: 元気 = well / healthy
Grammar: お + noun adds politeness; か marks question
Explanation: Literally, Are you well? More common when you have not seen someone for some time than as a daily greeting.

Hiragana: げんき です
Vocabulary: 元気 = well / energetic
Explanation: A simple polite response to お元気ですか.

Hiragana: だいじょうぶ です
English: It's okay / I'm fine / No thank you.
Vocabulary: 大丈夫 = okay / all right
Explanation: Very context-dependent. It can mean I'm okay, that's fine, or politely decline an offer.

Hiragana: わかりました
Vocabulary: 分かる = understand
Explanation: Literally understood. Common acknowledgement when someone gives instructions or information.

Hiragana: わかりません
English: I don't understand / I don't know.
Vocabulary: 分かる = understand
Explanation: Use when you do not understand something or do not know the answer.

Japanese: もう一度お願いします。
Hiragana: もう いちど おねがいします
Vocabulary: もう一度 = once more; お願いします = please
Grammar: request with お願いします
Explanation: A useful way to ask someone to repeat what they said.

Japanese: ゆっくり話してください。
Hiragana: ゆっくり はなして ください
Vocabulary: ゆっくり = slowly; 話す = speak
Grammar: て-form + ください = please do
Explanation: 話す becomes 話して, followed by ください to make a polite request.

Japanese: 日本語は少しだけ話せます。
Hiragana: にほんご は すこし だけ はなせます
English: I can speak only a little Japanese.
Vocabulary: 少し = a little; だけ = only; 話す = speak
Grammar: potential form 話せます = can speak
Explanation: A natural way to set expectations about your Japanese ability.

Hiragana: えいご は はなせますか
Vocabulary: 英語 = English; 話す = speak
Explanation: 話せます means can speak; か turns the polite statement into a question.

Hiragana: これは なんですか
Vocabulary: これ = this; 何 = what
Grammar: X は何ですか = what is X?
Explanation: One of the most useful basic question patterns.

Japanese: これはどういう意味ですか。
Hiragana: これは どういう いみ ですか
Romaji: Kore wa dō iu imi desu ka.
Vocabulary: どういう = what kind of; 意味 = meaning
Grammar: どういう意味 = what meaning
Explanation: Use when asking about a Japanese word, sign, sentence, or expression.

Japanese: 日本語で何と言いますか。
Hiragana: にほんご で なんと いいますか
Romaji: Nihongo de nan to iimasu ka.
English: How do you say it in Japanese?
Vocabulary: 日本語 = Japanese; 言う = say
Grammar: で = in/by means of; と = quotation marker
Explanation: Literally, What do you say [it] as in Japanese? Useful for learning vocabulary in context.

Hiragana: これを ください
Vocabulary: これ = this; ください = please give
Explanation: Point to an item and say this when buying or ordering.

Hiragana: これを おねがいします
Vocabulary: これ = this; お願いします = please
Explanation: Softer and very common when ordering food or requesting an item/service.

Hiragana: いくら ですか
Vocabulary: いくら = how much
Explanation: Standard way to ask the price.

Hiragana: かーど は つかえますか
Vocabulary: カード = card; 使う = use
Grammar: potential 使えます = can use
Explanation: Useful at shops and restaurants to ask whether cards are accepted.

Hiragana: げんきん だけ ですか
Vocabulary: 現金 = cash; だけ = only
Explanation: Ask this when you are unsure whether electronic or card payment is accepted.

Hiragana: ふくろ を おねがいします
Vocabulary: 袋 = bag
Explanation: Useful at convenience stores and supermarkets because shopping bags are often optional.

Hiragana: ふくろ は いりません
Vocabulary: 袋 = bag; 要る = need
Grammar: 要ります → 要りません = do not need
Explanation: A common response at checkout when you already have a bag.

Hiragana: れしーと を ください
Vocabulary: レシート = receipt
Explanation: A direct polite request for a receipt.

Japanese: これを試着してもいいですか。
Hiragana: これを しちゃくしても いいですか
Romaji: Kore o shichaku shite mo ii desu ka.
Vocabulary: 試着 = trying on clothes
Grammar: て-form + もいいですか = may I?
Explanation: A standard permission pattern: do X + is it okay?

Japanese: 別のサイズはありますか。
Hiragana: べつの さいず は ありますか
Romaji: Betsu no saizu wa arimasu ka.
Vocabulary: 別 = different; サイズ = size
Grammar: ありますか = is there / do you have
Explanation: Use in clothing or shoe shops to ask for another size.

Japanese: もう少し大きいサイズはありますか。
Hiragana: もう すこし おおきい さいず は ありますか
Romaji: Mō sukoshi ōkii saizu wa arimasu ka.
English: Do you have a slightly larger size?
Vocabulary: もう少し = a little more; 大きい = large
Grammar: ありますか = do you have
Explanation: もう少し modifies 大きい to mean a little larger.

Japanese: もう少し小さいサイズはありますか。
Hiragana: もう すこし ちいさい さいず は ありますか
Romaji: Mō sukoshi chiisai saizu wa arimasu ka.
English: Do you have a slightly smaller size?
Vocabulary: 小さい = small; サイズ = size
Grammar: ありますか = do you have
Explanation: The counterpart to asking for a larger size.

Hiragana: みている だけ です
Vocabulary: 見る = look; だけ = only
Explanation: Useful when shop staff approach and you do not need assistance yet.

Hiragana: めんぜい できますか
Vocabulary: 免税 = tax exemption
Grammar: できますか = can it be done?
Explanation: Useful at stores offering tax-free purchases to eligible visitors.

Hiragana: よやく しています
Vocabulary: 予約 = reservation
Explanation: At a restaurant or hotel, this naturally communicates that you already have a booking.

Hiragana: ふたり です
Vocabulary: 二人 = two people
Explanation: A natural short response when restaurant staff ask how many people are in your party.

Hiragana: ひとり です
Vocabulary: 一人 = one person
Explanation: Useful when entering a restaurant alone.

Japanese: メニューをお願いします。
Hiragana: めにゅー を おねがいします
Vocabulary: メニュー = menu
Explanation: A polite request for a menu.

Japanese: 英語のメニューはありますか。
Hiragana: えいご の めにゅー は ありますか
Romaji: Eigo no menyū wa arimasu ka.
English: Do you have an English menu?
Vocabulary: 英語 = English; メニュー = menu
Grammar: N の N = noun modifying noun
Explanation: 英語のメニュー literally means English-language menu.

Hiragana: おすすめ は なんですか
Vocabulary: おすすめ = recommendation; 何 = what
Explanation: A very useful restaurant and shopping question.

Hiragana: これに します
English: I'll have this / I'll choose this.
Vocabulary: これ = this
Grammar: N にします = decide on N
Explanation: A natural phrase for making your final choice from a menu or options.

Hiragana: みず を おねがいします
Vocabulary: 水 = water
Explanation: A polite way to request water.

Japanese: お会計をお願いします。
Hiragana: おかいけい を おねがいします
Vocabulary: お会計 = bill / checkout
Explanation: Use when you are ready to pay at a restaurant.

Hiragana: べつべつ に はらえますか
Vocabulary: 別々 = separately; 払う = pay
Grammar: potential 払えます = can pay
Explanation: Useful when asking whether a restaurant can split the bill.

Hiragana: いっしょ に はらいます
Vocabulary: 一緒に = together; 払う = pay
Explanation: Useful at checkout when staff ask whether payment is together or separate.

Japanese: 辛くしないでください。
Hiragana: からく しないで ください
Vocabulary: 辛い = spicy
Explanation: 辛い changes to 辛く before する; しないでください means please do not make/do.

Hiragana: にく は はいっていますか
Vocabulary: 肉 = meat; 入る = enter / be included
Explanation: Literally, Is meat in it? Useful for checking ingredients.

Hiragana: これは なま ですか
Vocabulary: 生 = raw / uncooked
Explanation: Useful when checking whether fish, egg, or meat is uncooked.

Hiragana: よく やいて ください
Vocabulary: よく = thoroughly; 焼く = grill/cook
Explanation: 焼く becomes 焼いて. Useful when requesting food to be well cooked.

Hiragana: おいしい です
Vocabulary: おいしい = delicious
Explanation: A simple polite compliment about food.

Hiragana: ごちそうさま でした
Vocabulary: ごちそうさま = thanks for the meal
Explanation: Commonly said after finishing a meal, including when leaving a restaurant.

Hiragana: えき は どこ ですか
Vocabulary: 駅 = station; どこ = where
Grammar: X はどこですか = where is X?
Explanation: A fundamental location question pattern.

Hiragana: といれ は どこ ですか
Vocabulary: トイレ = toilet; どこ = where
Explanation: One of the most practical phrases to memorize.

Hiragana: ここから とおい ですか
Vocabulary: ここ = here; から = from; 遠い = far
Explanation: Use when checking the distance to a destination.

Hiragana: あるいて いけますか
Vocabulary: 歩く = walk; 行く = go
Explanation: Literally, can [I] go by walking?

Japanese: どうやって行きますか。
Hiragana: どうやって いきますか
Vocabulary: どうやって = how; 行く = go
Explanation: Useful when asking which transport or route to take.

Japanese: この電車は東京駅に行きますか。
Hiragana: この でんしゃ は とうきょうえき に いきますか
Romaji: Kono densha wa Tōkyō-eki ni ikimasu ka.
English: Does this train go to Tokyo Station?
Vocabulary: 電車 = train; 駅 = station; 行く = go
Explanation: Replace 東京駅 with any station or destination.

Japanese: 次の電車は何時ですか。
Hiragana: つぎの でんしゃ は なんじ ですか
Romaji: Tsugi no densha wa nanji desu ka.
English: What time is the next train?
Vocabulary: 次 = next; 電車 = train; 何時 = what time
Explanation: A straightforward way to ask departure time.

Hiragana: なんばんせん ですか
Vocabulary: 何番線 = which track/platform
Explanation: At Japanese stations, 番線 refers to numbered railway tracks/platforms.

Japanese: この電車で合っていますか。
Hiragana: この でんしゃ で あっていますか
Romaji: Kono densha de atte imasu ka.
Vocabulary: 電車 = train; 合う = be correct
Grammar: 合っています = is correct
Explanation: Very useful when confirming you boarded or are about to board the correct train.

Japanese: どこで乗り換えますか。
Hiragana: どこで のりかえますか
Vocabulary: 乗り換える = transfer
Explanation: Ask where you need to change trains.

Japanese: 新宿まで何分かかりますか。
Hiragana: しんじゅく まで なんぷん かかりますか
English: How many minutes does it take to Shinjuku?
Vocabulary: まで = until/to; 何分 = how many minutes; かかる = take
Explanation: Replace 新宿 with your destination.

Hiragana: あいしーかーど は つかえますか
English: Can I use an IC card?
Vocabulary: ICカード = transit IC card; 使う = use
Explanation: Useful for buses, trains, shops, lockers, and other services.

Hiragana: ちゃーじ できますか
Vocabulary: チャージ = recharge / top up
Explanation: Common Japanese usage for adding money to an IC card or prepaid balance.

Hiragana: でぐち は どちら ですか
Vocabulary: 出口 = exit; どちら = which direction
Explanation: More polite than 出口はどこですか and natural when asking station staff.

Hiragana: みぎ です
Vocabulary: 右 = right
Explanation: A basic direction response.

Hiragana: ひだり です
Vocabulary: 左 = left
Explanation: A basic direction response.

Japanese: まっすぐ行ってください。
Hiragana: まっすぐ いって ください
Vocabulary: まっすぐ = straight; 行く = go
Explanation: A common direction instruction.

Japanese: ここで待ってもいいですか。
Hiragana: ここで まっても いいですか
Romaji: Koko de matte mo ii desu ka.
Vocabulary: 待つ = wait; ここ = here
Grammar: て-form + もいいですか = may I?
Explanation: で marks the place where waiting happens.

Japanese: ちょっと待ってください。
Hiragana: ちょっと まって ください
Vocabulary: ちょっと = a little; 待つ = wait
Explanation: Extremely common. 待つ changes to 待って.

Hiragana: いま なんじ ですか
Vocabulary: 今 = now; 何時 = what time
Grammar: 何時ですか = what time is it?
Explanation: A basic everyday time question.

Hiragana: きょう は なんにち ですか
Vocabulary: 今日 = today; 何日 = what date
Explanation: 何日 is read nannichi when asking the date.

Hiragana: きょう は あつい ですね
Vocabulary: 今日 = today; 暑い = hot
Explanation: Weather comments are common small talk. ね makes it shared/agreeable.

Hiragana: きょう は さむい ですね
Vocabulary: 寒い = cold
Explanation: A natural piece of casual small talk.

Hiragana: あめ が ふっています
Vocabulary: 雨 = rain; 降る = fall
Explanation: 降る becomes 降って. Literally, rain is falling.

Hiragana: かさ を もっていますか
Vocabulary: 傘 = umbrella; 持つ = have/carry
Grammar: 持っています = have / be carrying
Explanation: ている with 持つ commonly expresses possession.

Hiragana: きょう は しごと です
Vocabulary: 今日 = today; 仕事 = work
Explanation: Literally, as for today, [it] is work. Natural shorthand for having work today.

Hiragana: あした は やすみ です
Vocabulary: 明日 = tomorrow; 休み = day off
Explanation: Natural way to say tomorrow is your day off.

Hiragana: いま いそがしい ですか
Vocabulary: 今 = now; 忙しい = busy
Explanation: A polite, simple way to check whether someone has time.

Japanese: 少し時間がありますか。
Hiragana: すこし じかん が ありますか
English: Do you have a little time?
Vocabulary: 少し = a little; 時間 = time
Grammar: があります = there is / have
Explanation: Literally, is there a little time? A polite way to ask for someone's time.

Japanese: 手伝ってもらえますか。
Hiragana: てつだって もらえますか
Vocabulary: 手伝う = help; もらう = receive
Grammar: て-form + もらえますか = could I receive the favor?
Explanation: A polite and natural request for someone's help.

Hiragana: ちょっと かくにん します
Vocabulary: 確認 = confirmation/check; ちょっと = a moment
Explanation: Common at work and in service interactions when you need to verify something.

Hiragana: あとで れんらく します
Vocabulary: 後で = later; 連絡 = contact
Explanation: A useful work and social phrase for promising a later message/call.

Hiragana: めーる を おくりました
Vocabulary: メール = email; 送る = send
Explanation: 送ります becomes 送りました to say the action is completed.

Japanese: もう一度確認してください。
Hiragana: もう いちど かくにんして ください
Vocabulary: もう一度 = once again; 確認 = check
Explanation: A direct but polite request commonly useful at work.

Hiragana: もんだい ありません
Vocabulary: 問題 = problem; ある = exist
Explanation: Literally, there is no problem. Slightly more formal than 大丈夫です.

Hiragana: いい と おもいます
Vocabulary: いい = good; 思う = think
Explanation: The content before と is what you think: good + I think.

Hiragana: そう おもいます
Vocabulary: そう = so / that way; 思う = think
Explanation: A concise way to agree with an opinion.

Hiragana: ちょっと むずかしい です
Vocabulary: ちょっと = a little; 難しい = difficult
Explanation: In Japanese this can politely imply that something may not be possible, not merely that it is difficult.

Hiragana: できる と おもいます
English: I think I can do it / I think it's possible.
Vocabulary: できる = can do; 思う = think
Explanation: A useful way to express a tentative positive judgment.

Japanese: 今日はちょっと無理です。
Hiragana: きょう は ちょっと むり です
English: Today is a bit difficult / I can't today.
Vocabulary: 無理 = impossible / unreasonable
Explanation: A natural indirect way to decline plans for today.

Japanese: また今度お願いします。
Hiragana: また こんど おねがいします
English: Maybe next time / Please ask me again another time.
Vocabulary: また = again; 今度 = next time
Explanation: A friendly way to defer something to another occasion.

Hiragana: なにを していますか
Vocabulary: 何 = what; する = do
Explanation: The ongoing form of する asks what someone is currently doing.

Japanese: どこに住んでいますか。
Hiragana: どこに すんでいますか
Vocabulary: 住む = live; どこ = where
Grammar: に marks location; 住んでいます = live
Explanation: 住む changes to 住んで in the て-form.

Hiragana: とうきょう に すんでいます
Vocabulary: 東京 = Tokyo; 住む = live
Explanation: Use に, not で, with 住む for the place where you live.

Hiragana: どこから きましたか
Vocabulary: どこ = where; から = from; 来る = come
Explanation: Literally, From where did you come? Common when getting acquainted.

Hiragana: いんど から きました
Vocabulary: インド = India; から = from
Explanation: Literally, I came from India. A standard way to state where you are from.

Japanese: 日本に来てどのくらいですか。
Hiragana: にほん に きて どのくらい ですか
Romaji: Nihon ni kite dono kurai desu ka.
English: How long have you been in Japan?
Vocabulary: 日本 = Japan; どのくらい = how long
Explanation: Literally, after coming to Japan, about how long [has it been]?

Hiragana: さんかげつ ぐらい です
Vocabulary: 三か月 = three months; ぐらい = about
Explanation: A natural short answer to a question about how long.

Hiragana: にほん が すき です
Vocabulary: 日本 = Japan; 好き = liked/favorite
Explanation: Japanese 好き behaves like a na-adjective; the liked thing is commonly marked by が.

Japanese: 日本の生活に慣れました。
Hiragana: にほん の せいかつ に なれました
English: I've gotten used to life in Japan.
Vocabulary: 生活 = life; 慣れる = get used to
Grammar: に marks what you get used to
Explanation: 慣れました is the polite past and often implies the adjustment has happened.

Hiragana: まだ なれていません
English: I'm not used to it yet.
Vocabulary: まだ = still/yet; 慣れる = get used to
Grammar: ていません = not yet in state
Explanation: まだ plus negative naturally means not yet.

Hiragana: たのしい です
Vocabulary: 楽しい = fun / enjoyable
Explanation: A simple positive response about an experience or activity.

Hiragana: つかれました
Vocabulary: 疲れる = become tired
Explanation: Japanese commonly uses the past form 疲れました to express the resulting state: I got tired / I'm tired.

Hiragana: おなか が すきました
Vocabulary: お腹 = stomach; 空く = become empty
Explanation: Literally, my stomach became empty.

Hiragana: のど が かわきました
Vocabulary: 喉 = throat; 渇く = become dry
Explanation: Literally, my throat became dry.

Japanese: ちょっと休みたいです。
Hiragana: ちょっと やすみたい です
English: I'd like to rest a little.
Vocabulary: 休む = rest; ちょっと = a little
Grammar: verb stem + たい = want to
Explanation: 休み + たい expresses your desire to rest.

Japanese: 写真を撮ってもらえますか。
Hiragana: しゃしん を とって もらえますか
English: Could you take a photo for me?
Vocabulary: 写真 = photo; 撮る = take a photo
Grammar: て + もらえますか = could you do for me?
Explanation: A natural polite request to a stranger to take your photo.

Japanese: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。
Hiragana: ここで しゃしん を とっても いいですか
Romaji: Koko de shashin o totte mo ii desu ka.
Vocabulary: 写真 = photo; 撮る = take
Grammar: て + もいいですか = may I?
Explanation: Useful in temples, shops, museums, or other places where photography rules may vary.

Hiragana: わいふぁい は ありますか
Vocabulary: Wi-Fi = Wi-Fi; ある = exist
Explanation: A straightforward question at hotels, cafes, stations, and restaurants.

Japanese: パスワードは何ですか。
Hiragana: ぱすわーど は なんですか
Vocabulary: パスワード = password; 何 = what
Explanation: Often follows a question about Wi-Fi.

Japanese: 充電してもいいですか。
Hiragana: じゅうでん しても いいですか
Romaji: Jūden shite mo ii desu ka.
Vocabulary: 充電 = charging
Grammar: してもいいですか = may I do?
Explanation: A permission request for using a power outlet or charging point.

Japanese: コンセントはありますか。
Hiragana: こんせんと は ありますか
Vocabulary: コンセント = electrical outlet
Explanation: In Japanese, コンセント means a wall power outlet, not consent.

Hiragana: たすかりました
English: That was very helpful / You saved me.
Vocabulary: 助かる = be helped / saved
Explanation: A warm and natural way to thank someone whose help solved a problem.

Hiragana: きを つけて ください
Vocabulary: 気 = attention; つける = attach
Explanation: A common phrase for warning someone or wishing them safety.

Hiragana: また あいましょう
Vocabulary: また = again; 会う = meet
Explanation: A friendly phrase when parting from someone you expect or hope to see again.

Hiragana: またね
Vocabulary: また = again; ね = friendly particle
Explanation: Casual and friendly. Use with friends and people you are comfortable with, not formal situations.

Hiragana: おつかれさま です
English: Thanks for your hard work / Hello at work.
Vocabulary: お疲れさま = acknowledgment of effort
Explanation: Extremely common in Japanese workplaces. It can function as a greeting, acknowledgement, or thanks among colleagues.

Hiragana: おさきに しつれい します
English: Excuse me for leaving before you.
Vocabulary: お先に = before you; 失礼 = rudeness/excuse
Explanation: A standard phrase when leaving the workplace while others are still working.
